prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one full playable-room art-direction mockup for Tequila Kill, a top-down western game.
Primary request: DRAW THE COMPLETE SALOON SCENE WITH EXACTLY TWO CHARACTERS, PONCHO AND GARCIA, in the preferred soft-shaded pixel-art style of reference 1. Correct Poncho's floating appearance with convincing physical ground contact. A single wide 16:9 finished game-screen composition, no montage.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 is the MAIN APPROVED STYLE AND ROOM-SEED reference: retain its warm amber wood, cream plaster, blue-gray tiles, brick-red rug, chunky stair-step outlines, simplified pixel-art shapes and especially the SOFT SHADED VOLUMES the user explicitly prefers. Expand this small saloon corner into the entire saloon room. Do NOT turn it into harsh flat poster art, do not replace the gentle material shading with a strict flat palette.
Image 2 is CONTENT reference for the western setting and lived-in saloon only; do not copy its full outdoor map or its additional characters or markers.
Image 3 is CHARACTER IDENTITY reference: use ONLY the first two columns Poncho and Garcia. Ignore the experiment A/B characters, all text and all diagram panels.

CAMERA AND COMPOSITION:
A complete coherent saloon interior, roof removed as in an actual top-down Zelda-like room, framed from just beyond its room boundaries so the entire room reads. Orthographic horizontal/vertical room axes, overhead floor, short visible frontal faces on the back wall and furniture. Not isometric, not a dollhouse perspective, no cinematic foreshortening. The room fills the 16:9 image with no black margins or decorative border. Show the full back wall and two side walls with short unobtrusive lower wall sections and an open central threshold at the bottom. Warm cream plaster with dark timber posts, soft simple amber highlights, restrained gentle material gradients INSIDE hard pixelated silhouettes. Uniform coherent pixel-art detail density across architecture, furniture and both characters. Think a beautifully designed 16-bit overhead game room, hand-authored clusters and crisp stepped outlines, not a smooth vector drawing or high-detail painting reduced with a blur filter.

ROOM:
Expand the reference's L-shaped wooden counter into a full counter across the back-left part, rear bottle shelves and a few mugs, a couple of stools. Three modest card tables with chairs distributed along the sides, leaving generous clear navigable floor and crossing routes through the middle. One side table can have cards and red chips, another a bottle and mugs. A few clay pots, barrels and wooden crates at wall edges, a restrained brick-red rug with ochre geometric pattern at the entrance. All props belong to the same simplified chunky game-asset family as reference 1. Quiet desaturated blue-gray tiled floor, subtle low-contrast seams, minimal texture; the characters and furniture must stand out against it. No visual clutter, no noisy stone texture, no clutter over character silhouettes.

EXACTLY TWO CHARACTERS:
Poncho on the open lower-left/central part of the room, Garcia in the open upper-right/central part, both standing on the SAME floor, naturally separated by a few body widths. Similar readable body scale, each approximately 10 to 13 percent of image height. Neither character is an enlarged portrait or miniature icon. They aim toward one another from a slight diagonal while their bodies remain upright in the room's fixed top-down projection. Hands and weapons stay small.

PONCHO — IDENTITY AND THE CRITICAL CORRECTION:
Broad straw-gold oval sombrero with raised rounded olive crown, dark underside, long warm-brown poncho with ochre fringe, small hand and short revolver to his right. KEEP the cloth covering the feet, as previously requested by the user: do not expose boots or trousers. Crucially, he must feel firmly standing, not hovering. Show the cloth HANGING VERTICALLY under the hat with visible soft vertical folds and weight; the lower cloth gently flares and the short fringe RESTS AT THE FLOOR. Avoid the pointed levitating upside-down triangular/kite shape of reference 1. His lower silhouette has an irregular but broad resting hem, rather than one dangling sharp point. Let the lowest fringe pixels physically meet and partly occlude a NARROW DARK CONTACT SHADOW directly at the hem. No wide detached oval underneath, no blue floor gap between fabric and contact shadow, no long offset cast shadow suggesting height. The small shadow is compressed and attached, exactly like furniture feet, making his weight and floor level unambiguous. The user reported that he looks as if flying; resolve that unmistakably without changing the iconic hat or olive crown.

GARCIA:
Broad charcoal-gray hat with a small pale gold star emblem, blue-violet shoulders/sleeves, red neckerchief, dark trousers and compact dark boots visibly planted on the same floor. Small revolver aimed toward Poncho. These colors and silhouette make him immediately distinct. His short attached contact shadow uses the SAME light direction and floor plane as Poncho. No extra colored circle or character marker.

STYLE LOCK:
Preserve the friendly softly shaded pixel-art look of reference 1, confident dark stepped contours, simple readable geometry, gentle tonal variation within wood, pottery, cloth and hats, compact shaded volumes. Avoid overly coarse block abstractions, harsh black grid lines, blurred image edges, antialiasing, smeared textures, painterly fine detail, bloom and atmospheric haze. Soft material shading does not mean blurry silhouettes. Contact shadows are stronger and tighter than the broad soft-shaded surfaces.

NO TEXT, no logo, no HUD, no health bars, no ammo, no dash gauge, no J1/J2, no colored circles, no diamonds, no targeting markers, no muzzle flashes or projectiles, no dust puff under Poncho, no jumping or motion pose. Exactly two people, both visibly at rest and in contact with the floor. No bartender or background patrons. This is an art-direction mockup, not an engine screenshot or a sprite sheet.
intent: complete saloon art-direction mockup; soft-shaded preferred style; Poncho contact correction; no game integration
